claim.pdf_says:
Buginese:
1A00-1A16

[end of page 981] ... [top of page 982]

Buhid:
1740-1751
claim.why_it_matters: Same page-boundary defect: the label 'Buhid:' printed at the top of page 982 is attached to the Buginese range line ending page 981, orphaning the Buhid range 1740-1751 from its script name in normative Annex B.3.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against both rendered pages at 300 dpi. PDF p.1011 (printed 981) ends the body with exactly two lines, 'Buginese:' then '1A00-1A16', followed by whitespace and the footer '(c)ISO/IEC 2023   981'. Nothing else is printed after 1A00-1A16 -- there is no 'Buhid:' anywhere on that page. PDF p.1012 (printed 982) begins its body with 'Buhid:' then '1740-1751', then 'Canadian_Aboriginal:'. The markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md) instead reads at line 52 '1A00-1A16 Buhid:' inside the page-1011 slice, and the page-1012 slice (line 40241) opens with a bare '1740-1751'. So text printed on page 982 has been relocated into page 981's transcription and concatenated onto a different entry's data line. The claim misquotes neither source; both quoted strings match the sources verbatim. This is not hyphenation, not line wrapping within a paragraph, and not page-break furniture -- the page markers are separate lines and the label crossed them. Annex B is confirmed normative (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line ~40147: '## Annex B' / '(normative)'), so the claim's characterization of the location is correct. Refutation attempts that failed: (a) 'the text is still present' -- it is present, but on the wrong page and fused to the wrong entry, which is the definition of misplaced content for a per-page reconciliation; (b) 'only formatting' -- Annex B.3 is nothing but blank-line-delimited 'Script_Name:' / 'range-list' pairs, so the block boundary IS the semantic pairing, and the markdown yields the non-entities '1A00-1A16 Buhid:' and a nameless '1740-1751'. Verified as a systematic pattern rather than a one-off: the identical defect occurs at every Annex B.3 page boundary where the next page opens with a script label -- 6 instances in the annex ('1E900-1E943, 1E94B Ahom:', '1A00-1A16 Buhid:', 'A984-A9B2 Kaithi:', '10600-10736, 10740-10755, 10760-10767 Linear_B:', '10980-1099F Miao:', '10C80-10CB2, 10CC0-10CF2 Old_Italic:'). Page 1011 is itself a victim of the same bug at its leading edge: its markdown opens with a bare '11700-1171A' because 'Ahom:' was pulled up onto page 1010's last line, while the PDF plainly prints 'Ahom:' above '11700-1171A' on page 981.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, but the impact statement overstates the harm. The script name 'Buhid:' is not lost and the reading order is not scrambled: reading the markdown linearly (ignoring the interposed page anchor and running header) still yields Buginese -> 1A00-1A16 -> Buhid -> 1740-1751, so a human reader recovers the correct pairing and no characters are dropped. The genuine defect is placement, not loss: a label printed at the top of page 982 was transcribed onto the final line of page 981, fusing it to the preceding entry's range list and splitting the Buhid name/range block across the page boundary. The concrete risk is to automated extraction -- any parser that derives the XID_Start repertoire by splitting Annex B.3 on blank lines gets a malformed record '1A00-1A16 Buhid:' and an unnamed range '1740-1751'. Severity is fairly rated structural (block structure is wrong) but the content is recoverable, so it is low-consequence for prose reading. It should be ledgered as one instance of a systematic page-boundary artifact affecting all 6 Annex B.3 page breaks, and fixed as a class rather than per page; note that page 1011's own first entry is missing its 'Ahom:' label for the identical reason.
